- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price action (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model misaligns with mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day rolling average of price.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid false bullishness.
